cases.requirement: M4-051 preserves Spec 0027 authority: recognized bash/pwsh command text remains opaque SHELL_COMMAND evidence and the enclosing accepted shell call classifies as process.exec only.

The negative boundary concerns a string-level matcher used to infer a nested shell effect; it does not claim that the enclosing recognized shell process escaped process.exec classification or ToolRuntime governance.
Repository architecture explicitly warns that equivalent shell spellings can bypass a string-level matcher and forbids Shell String as the sole security semantic.
The Gate-local LITERAL_DENY_SUBSTRING_V1 matcher performs exact substring presence only and does not trim, normalize, tokenize, parse, expand, emulate or execute shell text.
The matcher configuration and literal are fixed before evaluating the reference and alternative spellings and are not adapted after observing the alternative command.
The reference and alternative shell spellings are distinct exact strings; supplying the same command twice cannot establish equivalent-spelling bypass evidence.
For the same fixed matcher, the reference spelling yields MATCH and the measured-effect-equivalent alternative yields NO_MATCH.
Each measured shell execution operates only on a test-owned disposable temporary target and proves its exact sentinel is absent immediately before that isolated execution.
Both measured spellings use the same fixed synthetic non-secret payload and M4-051 does not require access to credentials, user secrets, production files or unrelated repository data.
In a supported reference environment, the reference spelling succeeds and produces the exact expected benign sentinel bytes.
In the separately reset target state, the alternative spelling succeeds and produces exactly the same expected benign sentinel bytes as the reference spelling.
Measured-effect equivalence is established from exact controlled observations rather than from textual similarity or an unsupported claim of universal shell-program semantic equivalence.
When ESSM-005 through ESSM-012 are coherently proven for one supported witness, the exact Gate-local classification is EXPECTED_STRING_MATCHER_BYPASS.

EXPECTED_STRING_MATCHER_BYPASS is a negative test/evidence classification and must not be relabeled as ALLOW, DENY, UNCLASSIFIED, EXPECTED_UNGOVERNED, SANDBOXED, TOOL_ENFORCED, PROVIDER_ENFORCED or PROCESS_ISOLATED.
A NO_MATCH result from the test-only matcher is never policy allow and must not be retroactively represented as a CapabilityDecision, Lease, Receipt, approval or audit authorization fact.
A matcher false negative does not erase or downgrade the enclosing process.exec requirement and does not prove that the accepted M4-040/M4-041 ToolRuntime guard was bypassed.
If the required controlled shell or writable disposable target is unavailable because of an external CI/OS/container restriction, the result is ENVIRONMENT_UNSUPPORTED rather than safe-runtime DENY.
An ENVIRONMENT_UNSUPPORTED-only matrix cannot accept M4-051; at least one exact-head supported environment must produce EXPECTED_STRING_MATCHER_BYPASS.

Contradictory or incomplete matcher results, identical commands, pre-existing target state, mismatched bytes, differing measured effects, secret-bearing targets or false process-governance claims are INVALID_EVIDENCE and fail conformance.
M4-051 must not add, widen or recommend a production raw-command substring/regex/word-list matcher, quote stripper, shell canonicalizer or parser merely to change the expected negative result.
M4-051 makes no shell-parser completeness claim; shell effects may depend on language semantics, executables, sourced code, variables, environment and providers outside a lexical matcher.

M4-051 remains distinct from M4-050: M4-050 measures direct host API behavior outside ToolRuntime, while M4-051 preserves process.exec governance and measures incompleteness of nested-effect inference from raw shell spelling.

Harness-specific assertions about recognized shell tool dispatch or ToolRuntime control flow use only pinned 0.1.0-rc.5 commit 47f943859bef60e4160492346772ded9b24f765a; Harness does not become portable shell-language authority.

The protocol-first M4-051 delta contains exactly the candidate Spec, this requirement corpus and CURRENT handoff state; it contains no production/executable tests, dependency/lockfile, schema/protocol wire, Shared TCK, workflow, HISTORY, roadmap acceptance marker, M4-052+ implementation or PR merge.
